name: Love Muscle

tenures.source: Won a tag match on the season-opening card, then the World Tag Team Championship at "Take No Prisoners."

caption: A self-declared tag team of two singles stars who won the World Tag Team Championship at the promotion's own "Take No Prisoners" special before drifting apart mid-year.

name: Alliance of Violence

tenures.source: Billed entering "Take No Prisoners" as the promotion's own World Tag Team Champions of four months' standing; lost the title there to Love Muscle.

caption: A tag team billed as the promotion's own only World Tag Team Champions for four months before losing the title to Love Muscle at "Take No Prisoners."

identity.note: Shares a bare unit name with an already-held tag team of a different promotion; no operator, roster or storyline axis ties the two.

name: Team Tradition
caption: A debuting tag team that won the opening round of the promotion's own Tag Team Championship tournament.

tenures.source: Debuted and won the opening round of the promotion's own Tag Team Championship tournament, advancing to the second round.

name: Precious Moments
caption: A comedic fairy-themed tag team that upset the ACWA Heavyweight Champion and a former champion in the opening round of the promotion's own Tag Team Championship tournament, only for the champion to turn on his own partner afterward.

tenures.source: Debuted, defeating ACWA Heavyweight Champion "Showstoppa" Steve Starr and Chad Shakespeare in the opening round of the promotion's own Tag Team Championship tournament, advancing to the second round.

identity.note: A same-named tag act is on file at an unrelated 2002 website promotion; different medium, different form (a two-person unit here against a solo character there), no operator or roster overlap.

name: Towers of Havoc
caption: Two masked, seven-foot wrestlers managed by Howie Harding, who debuted by squashing the Pain Brothers well past the finish ahead of the promotion's own Tag Team Championship tournament.

tenures.source: Debuted with a disqualification win over the Pain Brothers on the promotion's own 18 December 1999 house show, then appeared at ringside four days later scouting the promotion's own Tag Team Championship tournament.

name: The Pain Brothers
caption: A jobber tag team battered by the debuting Towers of Havoc.

tenures.source: Lost to the debuting Towers of Havoc by disqualification on the promotion's own 18 December 1999 house show.
Lost a tag match to Corrupted Morals at Jersey Jack Grappling's first house show.

name: Pony Express
caption: An unnamed tag team that squashed a jobber duo in the opening match of a December 1999 house show.

tenures.source: Defeated a jobber tag team in the opening match of the 11 December 1999 house show with a double clothesline finisher.

name: The Sulkeys
caption: A jobber tag team of two brothers squashed in the opening match of a December 1999 house show.

tenures.source: Lost the opening match of the 11 December 1999 house show to a debuting tag team.

name: Fat Man and Little Boy
caption: A short-lived tag team pairing of two wrestlers who debuted together for the predecessor promotion in December 1999 before working separately for Jersey Jack Grappling.

tenures.source: Lost to Precious Moments on the 11 December 1999 house show.
